name: Boeing E-3G Sentry (USAF AWACS, present day)

published.source: USAF E-3 Sentry fact sheet: length 145 ft 6 in (44.35 m), wingspan 145 ft 9 in (44.4 m), height 41 ft 4 in (12.6 m); rotodome 30 ft (9.1 m) across and 6 ft (1.83 m) deep, held 11 ft (3.35 m) above the fuselage by two struts

engine_contract.row: js/hero/us_e3_sentry.js registers nine rows from one builder (HeroE3.build with a per-row spec): nato_e80_awacs, nato_e00_awacs, awacs_n, nato_e90_awacs (E-8C), gbr_e90_awacs, gbr_e00_awacs, awacs_f, fra_e90_awacs, fra_e00_awacs
engine_contract.current_nodes: one 'gear' group (the renderer stows it), the lowest opaque part, wheels on z = -3.45
engine_contract.len_rule: UNIT_MODELS[key].len = the measured X extent (44.35 m for the E-3 rows, 46.6 m for the E-8C)

references.name: [P1] USAF E-3 from above, 2009
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'Boeing E-3 Sentry 090512-F-7550B-902.jpg' (USAF, public domain), 1280 px thumbnail
references.note: Plan-ish view from above and behind the port wing. Shows: the rotodome's two radar halves near-black, a pale band about a quarter of the diameter (2.3 m) wide straight across its centre with toothed edges and pale rib lines running about 1 m from one band edge into the dark half [P1, P2]; the dome centred over the wing's trailing edge root; all-over white/very light grey paint; the four slim pods ahead of the wing on raked pylons; the raked fin with its dorsal fillet; the low tailplane. Not scaled: perspective.

references.name: [P2] E-3G at Prince Sultan AB, 1 March 2020
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'E-3G aircrew disembark their aircraft at Prince Sultan Air Base, 1 March 2020.jpg' (USAF, public domain), 1280 px thumbnail
references.note: From under the port wing, looking forward-starboard. Shows: the dome edge-on - dark at both ends, pale in the middle, so the band ran athwartships at that moment (the dome turns in service); the two broad struts, white; the four-wheel main bogies; the port entry door aft (open); white overall. Not scaled: close, wide-angle perspective.

must_show: the rotodome: a lens 9.1 m across and about 1.8 m deep, centred 28.5 m aft of the nose (x -6.33), bottom at z 5.53, top at z 7.33
the dome's paint: two near-black radar halves either side of a pale band 2.3 m wide across its centre (x -7.48 .. -5.18, laid athwartships), over the upper face, the rim and the lower face
two struts under the dome, the forward one broader, at x -4.6 .. -6.6 and -6.8 .. -8.6, from the crown (z 2.1) to the dome (z 5.5)
the 707 body: 3.76 m wide, level crown at z 2.13 from 7.5 m to 31 m aft of the nose, belly rising aft of x -9
the wing swept about 35 degrees, leading edge from x 8.4 at the root to x -7.0 at the tip, tips at y +-22.2, z +1.25
four slim TF33 pods hung well ahead of the wing on raked pylons, 10.1 m and 16.0 m off the centreline, their lips at about x 9.0 (inboard) and x 4.2 (outboard)
the raked fin with a dorsal fillet from x -10.4, tip at z 9.15 near x -19.5; the low tailplane 14.2 m across at z 0.7 .. 1.5, x -15.8 .. -22.1
four-wheel main bogies 22.5 m aft of the nose (x -0.33) at y +-3.4; twin nose wheels at x 16.9
all-over white / very light grey paint over the whole airframe (x -22.2 .. 22.2), plain (no markings); team colour in the ring near the dome's rim, the wingtips, tailplane tips and fin tip

the pale rib lines off one band edge and the toothed band edges ([P1], [P2]): the model draws dark ticks inside the band instead; their count and spacing are not measured
the strut stations and widths: from the three-view and the Souda Bay photograph named in the hero header, not from [P1] or [P2]
